jiangbai.contact.card_usage: Call 27571 to have the Mysterious Contact clear your current crime count and investigation evidence. A successful cleanup starts a 10-day cooldown. No records to clear or hanging up early uses no cooldown. Officers already dispatched and penalties already imposed are unaffected.

serverroom.daily.settlement_fault: Server room settlement failed. Saving and trading are paused; check the log.
serverroom.daily.sleep_not_ready: Server room data or an asset transaction is not ready. Try resting again shortly.

security.box.large.flavor: Security always gets hold of interesting things, don't you think?

npc.refusal.lower.bottleneck: The CPU and GPU in this bottleneck build cannot keep up. I won't buy it.
npc.refusal.vesper.bottleneck: That build is unbalanced. Upgrade the CPU and GPU, then come back.
npc.purchase.vesper.rules: I buy intact PC parts. Complete PCs, Value Builds and Bottleneck Builds are welcome too, provided the case and every installed part are intact T1-T3. No unfinished cases.
npc.refusal.upper.low_tier: I only buy intact T3 or higher configurations.
save.unsupported: This version requires a valid save-generation marker of 2.6 or higher. Old saves are not migrated or overwritten. Continue 1.0 saves with the retained 2.3.1 version.
supplier.thief.name: PC Parts Thief
supplier.thief.greeting: Picked up some high-tier PC parts. Some are pristine, some took a knock. You know your hardware; take your pick.
supplier.thief.offer: Everything is on the counter. Don't ask where it came from; just see if there's anything you need.

flavor.component_cooler.t1.broken: The fins have been crushed together. Where air once passed, there is only metal.
flavor.component_cooler.t1.intact: Its first installer studied the mounting clips for half an hour. The instructions were right by their feet.
flavor.component_cooler.t2.broken: The mounting bracket bends sideways. The two towers no longer line up, like neighbors after an argument.
flavor.component_cooler.t2.intact: Two towers side by side. The builder measures first to see whether the case panel will still close.
flavor.component_cooler.t3.broken: A heat pipe has kinked sharply. All that weight failed to protect the most delicate part.
flavor.component_cooler.t3.intact: Lift it and you understand why a cooler might need a little support of its own.
flavor.component_cooler.t4.broken: A hose fitting has split. A dried trail of coolant runs down to the radiator's lower edge.
flavor.component_cooler.t4.intact: From a copper base to a full radiator. The builder now has to find seating for the hoses.
flavor.component_cooler.t5.broken: A diagonal crack crosses the screen and the pump housing is chipped. The polished face has finally come apart.
flavor.component_cooler.t5.intact: Even the cooler has a little screen. There is more to look at inside the case than on the desk.
flavor.component_cpu.t1.broken: A corner has chipped off the substrate. The lettering on the lid is in much better shape.
flavor.component_cpu.t1.intact: Once kept office hours alongside its user. Its most frequent instruction was probably 'save'.
flavor.component_cpu.t2.broken: A deep gouge cuts across the underside, interrupting a path through the dense contacts.
flavor.component_cpu.t2.intact: Never in the most expensive column, but remembered from plenty of first builds.
flavor.component_cpu.t3.broken: Heat has browned the edge of the lid. The seller's claim of heavy workloads suddenly carries some weight.
flavor.component_cpu.t3.intact: Bought for work, supposedly. The first thing launched after assembly was a game.
flavor.component_cpu.t4.broken: The substrate crack runs beneath the lid. A fingertip-sized fracture has swallowed a considerable budget.
flavor.component_cpu.t4.intact: On its first boot, the owner watched the temperature so long that the original plan slipped away.
flavor.component_cpu.t5.broken: The lid has shifted, exposing a gap. Advanced fabrication is still vulnerable to an ordinary hard knock.
flavor.component_cpu.t5.intact: The model name keeps getting longer. The chip stays small; the bill does not.
flavor.component_fan.t1.broken: Half a blade is missing. The others still look dutifully ready for work.
flavor.component_fan.t1.intact: When it spins up on the test bench, the paper scraps notice it starting work before the shopkeeper does.
flavor.component_fan.t2.broken: The frame has split around a screw hole. Tightening things harder is clearly not always the answer.
flavor.component_fan.t2.intact: One screw was missing from the bag. The shopkeeper supplied another in a different color.
flavor.component_fan.t3.broken: The hub sits crooked. Blades have scraped a half-circle into the frame. The silence came afterward.
flavor.component_fan.t3.intact: You have to lean close to hear it running. The old hard drive beside it suddenly seems very talkative.
flavor.component_fan.t4.broken: The broken blade ends in a ragged stump. The familiar color scheme makes the damage hard to miss.
flavor.component_fan.t4.intact: Someone always dislikes this color scheme. Someone else comes looking specifically for it.
flavor.component_fan.t5.broken: The light ring is cracked and the blades jammed. Its last appearance probably was not on a display stand.
flavor.component_fan.t5.intact: One costs as much as several ordinary fans. The customer still wants a whole case full.
flavor.component_gpu.t1.broken: A broken fan blade lies inside the shroud. Years of matches ended with a single drop.
flavor.component_gpu.t1.intact: An old companion for old games. Lower the settings a little and everyone gets along.
flavor.component_gpu.t2.broken: The bracket is twisted and the board edge cracked. The seller insists it was just a bump in transit.
flavor.component_gpu.t2.intact: The buyer examines it three times, then asks how much will be left for food this month.
flavor.component_gpu.t3.broken: A piece of the shroud is missing. The exposed board carries a troubling patch of brown scorch.
flavor.component_gpu.t3.intact: Still rendering in the background, already gaming in the foreground. Its last owner knew how to spend a wait.
flavor.component_gpu.t4.broken: The heavy heatsink has warped the board. All that performance did nothing to soften the landing.
flavor.component_gpu.t4.intact: The long card reaches past the motherboard. The cables need to relocate before it can move in.
flavor.component_gpu.t5.broken: Charred black covers the components. The model is recognizable; nobody wants to name a price first.
flavor.component_gpu.t5.intact: Whenever it is on the counter, every ring of the doorbell makes the shopkeeper look up to see who is coming.
flavor.component_hdd.t1.broken: A dent sits right over the platter. The small rattle inside is not a sound you want to hear twice.
flavor.component_hdd.t1.intact: Nothing vast. Enough for years of documents and a few old games you cannot bring yourself to delete.
flavor.component_hdd.t2.broken: A corner of the connector is missing. A few millimeters of broken contact now separate you from the data.
flavor.component_hdd.t2.intact: Every file named 'final version' somehow has room for one more revision here.
flavor.component_hdd.t3.broken: A black burn marks the underside board. The fate of dozens of folders is suddenly uncertain.
flavor.component_hdd.t3.intact: Room for people who keep every file. Sorting them is a job for another day.
flavor.component_hdd.t4.broken: A deep gouge cuts into the edge. Somewhere, an all-night server room is down one shift worker.
flavor.component_hdd.t4.intact: Pulled from a rack whose lights never went out. Retirement looks more like a shift change.
flavor.component_hdd.t5.broken: The split seal tells its own story. Nobody will vouch for whatever once lived inside.
flavor.component_hdd.t5.intact: Print out everything it could hold and the shop's shelving would have to move out first.
flavor.component_motherboard.t1.broken: A corner has snapped off. Exposed copper traces end abruptly, like roads leading nowhere.
flavor.component_motherboard.t1.intact: Pulled from a little office PC. It still seems to carry the drowsiness of a Monday morning.
flavor.component_motherboard.t2.broken: A shard of plastic sits in a cracked slot. Whoever pulled the part out missed the release latch.
flavor.component_motherboard.t2.intact: The box is gone, but the build list survives. Its line is the only one that was never crossed out.
flavor.component_motherboard.t3.broken: The power section is scorched brown. Beneath the heatsink lies an accident omitted from the invoice.
flavor.component_motherboard.t3.intact: The traces wind neatly around every screw hole. Better organized than the ledger behind the counter.
flavor.component_motherboard.t4.broken: A crack runs beneath the armor. All that imposing metal cannot conceal the severed traces.
flavor.component_motherboard.t4.intact: The heatsink armor dominates the board. You have to lean closer to find the model name.
flavor.component_motherboard.t5.broken: Several rows of socket contacts lean sideways. Even the damage is too precise to see at a glance.
flavor.component_motherboard.t5.intact: After hearing the price, the customer asks again: is that for the board or the whole computer?
flavor.component_psu.t1.broken: A black scorch ring surrounds the cable exit. The smell of burnt plastic still lingers.
flavor.component_psu.t1.intact: The least remarkable metal box in the case decides when every other part wakes up.
flavor.component_psu.t2.broken: The cable bundle is neatly tied. The plugs at the far end have melted together.
flavor.component_psu.t2.intact: The '0' and '1' on the switch once puzzled a beginner enough to bring the builder back.
flavor.component_psu.t3.broken: The casing has a deep dent. Something small rolls around inside whenever it moves.
flavor.component_psu.t3.intact: Whoever removed it coiled each cable separately. For once, no untangling is required.
flavor.component_psu.t4.broken: A scorch mark runs across the intake. Expensive cables did nothing to prevent whatever happened.
flavor.component_psu.t4.intact: A dot of red paint marks one connector: a reminder not to put that cable in the wrong place again.
flavor.component_psu.t5.broken: The nameplate still shines like a mirror. The seller put the burnt side face down.
flavor.component_psu.t5.intact: A discreet model name, in packaging that treats it like classified equipment.
flavor.component_ram.t1.broken: One contact has chipped away, leaving a gap in an otherwise orderly row of gold.
flavor.component_ram.t1.intact: Remembers everything the programs need all day. Forgets it all the moment the power goes off.
flavor.component_ram.t2.broken: The board has acquired an unwanted curve. A low price will not make the slot any more forgiving.
flavor.component_ram.t2.intact: The seller says you will feel better with another stick. He tells every customer that.
flavor.component_ram.t3.broken: One chip has cracked open. The exposed fracture lies beyond the heat spreader's protection.
flavor.component_ram.t3.intact: Several large programs can finally share the room without asking someone else to leave.
flavor.component_ram.t4.broken: One end of the spreader has peeled away, exposing missing components. The bundle's value came apart with it.
flavor.component_ram.t4.intact: Once one of a pair, now on its own. Its partner is probably busy in another computer.
flavor.component_ram.t5.broken: A scorch crosses several chips. The handsome casing now serves only to earn a second glance.
flavor.component_ram.t5.intact: The capacity is printed large, the price small. A familiar trick on this counter.
flavor.computer_case.t1.broken: One corner took a hard hit. The panel is keeping its secrets better than the seller did.
flavor.computer_case.t1.intact: The thin panels let the fans do the talking. Still, every first build needs a home.
flavor.computer_case.t2.broken: The panel has buckled and cables poke through the gap. Moving day clearly went badly.
flavor.computer_case.t2.intact: The cables tuck away behind the tray. One less tangled mess under the desk.
flavor.computer_case.t3.broken: The front frame is bent and the feet no longer line up. It insists on the counter's flattest spot.
flavor.computer_case.t3.intact: Black panels, straight lines, no fuss. It looks reassuring next to the rest of the stock.
flavor.computer_case.t4.broken: Cracks divide the display panel into fragments. Somehow, the view inside is worse than before.
flavor.computer_case.t4.intact: Behind all that glass, every cable is on display. There is nowhere to hide a sloppy build.
flavor.computer_case.t5.broken: One corner has caved in. The rest still has the imposing bulk of a building awaiting demolition.
flavor.computer_case.t5.intact: It takes up half the counter. The shopkeeper is reconsidering the policy of paying per item.

text.01fc8dc622e5: Displaying this sign raises the PC Materials Seller's daily visit chance from 30% to 75%, and the PC Parts Thief's from 15% to 30%. The seller is eligible from day 5 and the thief from day 12. Multiple signs do not stack. Each visit is rolled separately when the shop opens; successful visitors join the end of the day's queue and are not shown in the vanilla Expected Normal Customers list. Displaying intact T4 or T5 parts can still attract the PC Buyer.
text.055f6bdf0038: Here are the parts and materials. See anything you need?
text.150a32bc88cf: All memory sticks must be the same tier
text.2fe62616a758: Once it lights up, people carrying bags of spare parts know which door to try.
text.34ccec0329de: Obtain Vesper's 0504 business card once to unlock calls to her permanently.
text.39c95467b293: You must own the teardown screwdriver to use it.
text.3ed437206a5f: Part tiers are more than three steps apart
text.3f2ae7609f09: Got decent parts or a tidy value build? I'll take a look.
text.47b2c0f573a3: Found a few working PC parts. Brought screws and electronic parts too; they're always handy for repairs.
text.4887c4447d04: I buy working PC parts and qualifying complete builds up to T3.
text.4c405ee461f5: Unlock failed. Check the game log.
text.5eb52273543e: This case is jammed. Use the teardown screwdriver to open it.
text.69e3a29d2368: Remove the part from the PC case before repairing it.
text.6a7bc1081071: I can't afford parts this good.
text.723b3b1739c9: Found these on my rounds. See anything you like? I stop by every Friday if you want to trade.
text.72e9b91a379f: You can only unlock a PC case you own.
text.79392d2f43d1: I buy working PC parts and complete builds up to T3. No bottleneck builds or half-empty cases.
text.8bf853ae1d76: Sure, I'll bring a few rigs over. See you at the shop.
text.8d59d9e16dff: I've got a spare tower gathering dust. Make me an offer.
text.996b4925c50c: Build data could not be synchronized. Close and reopen the case, then test again.
text.a3ec80c70209: I've got cash to spend and a few towers to sell. Anything catch your eye? You can disassemble and assemble parts in the workroom.
text.ab200af82511: You do not own a locked PC case.
text.b18ca73d66e9: Unlocked. Double-click the case to retrieve its parts.
text.b7bb85ea4318: You can only use this while at the shop.
text.bb9a3627859b: That'll do. Let's agree on a price.
text.c9eaa60d077e: I only buy working T3+ PC parts. Complete builds must have every required part, and every installed part must be working and at least T3.
text.da4324746524: Show me the good stuff. I don't deal in anything below T3.
text.e53d5207f70f: This PC case is not locked.
text.e8ccfb408f51:
Vesper's number: 0504. Buying or actually owning this card once permanently unlocks calls and shopping with her, even if you lose it. A shop visit or card offer alone does not unlock the contact. Phone visits have a three-day cooldown. The lower-district builder who sells this card stops by every Friday.
Mod QQ group: 157249439

luoxi.story.offer_1: Things have been a bit tense with Security lately. I can't keep this lot at my shop anymore.
luoxi.story.offer_2: Not exactly clean goods, but good stuff. Hold on to it for me. I'll come back in a few days.
luoxi.story.accept: All right. I'll hold it for three days.
luoxi.story.accepted: Here's the list. Store it however you like, but when I return, I want the same goods and every original part inside.
luoxi.story.refused: Fine, no pressure. We can still do business.
luoxi.story.first: Three days are up. Things are mostly sorted on my end. Let's have my goods back.
luoxi.story.final: It's been another two days. Can I have my goods back this time?
luoxi.story.first_missing: Still not ready? I'll come back in a couple of days, then.
luoxi.story.failed_2: Never mind. We can still do business.
luoxi.story.complete_1: All present and accounted for. All right, I owe you one.
luoxi.story.complete_2: Take this GPU. If you need parts, order them on the server room PC and I'll drop them off. Everything I sell you is ten percent off from now on.
luoxi.story.unlocked: All original goods returned. Intact T4 GPU awarded; daily parts orders unlocked; shared order limit raised from 3 to 5; permanent 10% discount on Vesper's goods.
luoxi.story.reward_pending: Your GPU is set aside. Make inventory space and collect it when Vesper visits the shop.
luoxi.story.counter_full: I need to hand over the whole lot at once. Clear enough counter and inventory space, then come back for it.
luoxi.story.receive: There's room now. Accept the whole shipment.
luoxi.story.missing: Missing or in the wrong condition: {0}. Remove parts installed in other machines first. The original goods and all original internal parts must be intact.
luoxi.story.keeping: Keep it safe for now. Hand it back when I return.
luoxi.story.recovery: The handover is still being verified. Please try again shortly.
luoxi.transfer.busy: The goods are being checked. Please try again shortly.
luoxi.transfer.counter_full: The counter cannot hold the entire shipment. Clear enough space first.
luoxi.transfer.inventory_full: Your inventory cannot hold this shipment. Clear enough space first.
luoxi.transfer.identity_conflict: The stored goods' identities need verification. They cannot be collected again yet.
jiangbai.story.offer_1: Tch. Got myself into a bit of trouble these last few days.
jiangbai.story.offer_2: Hey, let me hide out here for a few days.
jiangbai.story.offer_3: I'll give you something before I leave.
jiangbai.story.accept: All right. You can stay here.
jiangbai.story.farewell_1: Thanks for these past few days.
jiangbai.story.farewell_2: That lousy server room is way too loud.
jiangbai.story.farewell_3: Here's a number. Call it next time you're in trouble. Whoever answers will sort it out.
jiangbai.contact.name: Mysterious Contact

smallstory.L1-001: You keep these broken parts pretty well sorted.
smallstory.L1-002: I've seen people dump everything in a corner. Two days later, even they can't tell what's what.
smallstory.L1-003: What are you planning to do with all this?
smallstory.L1-101: Take it apart, fix it up, then sell it.
smallstory.L1-103: Nothing wrong with giving it a proper going-over.
smallstory.L1-201: It's all business. Whatever makes money.
smallstory.L1-203: In our line of work, every credit takes some earning.
smallstory.L1-901: Fix what you can, toss what you can't. Don't hang on to useless junk.
smallstory.L2-001: An old customer brought his PC in again a couple of days ago.
smallstory.L2-002: Dead PSU. The rest is fine, and he doesn't want to replace the whole thing.
smallstory.L2-003: I'm short of a suitable one. Got a T1 PSU here?
smallstory.L2-004: One you've repaired is fine, or any suitable replacement. I'll pay the usual buying price.
smallstory.L2-101: Sure. I'll keep an eye out.
smallstory.L2-103: He just wants a few more years out of his old friend.
smallstory.L2-201: I'm too busy at the moment. I don't think I can help.
smallstory.L2-203: Don't let it get in the way of your own work.
smallstory.L2-301: Found that PSU we talked about?
smallstory.L2-302: Here it is. Take a look.
smallstory.L2-304: No rush. Just don't bring me a broken one to make up the numbers.
smallstory.L2-311: You've been paid for the PSU.
smallstory.L2-312: Take these materials too. Something for your trouble.
smallstory.L2-320: I need an intact T1 PSU. Keep looking.
smallstory.L2-321: Hold on. The goods and payment aren't settled yet. Let's try again in a bit.
smallstory.L2-330: The PSU is paid for. I'll hold the materials until you've made room.
smallstory.L2-331: There's room now. I'll take the materials.
smallstory.L2-333: Still no room. I'll keep them for now.
smallstory.L2-314: I'll fit it when I get back. Maybe he'll stop asking me every day.
smallstory.L3-001: That shipment from last time is all sorted.
smallstory.L3-003: Were you tempted to open it up and have a look while you had it?
smallstory.L3-101: I kept everything by the list. Didn't dare touch it.
smallstory.L3-103: Looks like I picked the right person.
smallstory.L3-201: I had a look inside, then put everything back.
smallstory.L3-203: As long as it came back as it was, how you stored it is your business.
smallstory.L3-902: Enough about that. Let's see today's goods.
smallstory.L3-301: That storage job I asked you about? I made other arrangements.
smallstory.L3-302: No need to keep worrying about it.
smallstory.L3-306: It really wasn't a good time for me back then.
smallstory.L3-401: Looking to buy today, or have you got something to sell?
smallstory.L3-402: I let you down last time.
smallstory.L3-404: From now on, we settle goods and payment face to face. Saves us both the trouble.
smallstory.L4-002: Had some repair materials to spare. Brought a share over on my way past.
smallstory.L4-003: You'll always find a use for them here.
smallstory.L4-101: I'll take them, then. How much?
smallstory.L4-102: If I wanted payment, I'd have put them on the counter.
smallstory.L4-103: Take them. Just try dropping a couple fewer on the floor next time.
smallstory.L4-201: You need them too. Keep them.
smallstory.L4-203: Fine, I'll take them back. No need to keep being polite about it.
smallstory.L4-301: Make some room first. I'll keep this lot for you.
smallstory.L4-302: There's room now. I'll take them.
smallstory.L4-303: Here. Don't ask me for more if you lose them.
smallstory.L4-304: Still not enough space. I'll hold them for now.
smallstory.L4-901: You've already had that lot. Don't pretend you've forgotten.
smallstory.L5-002: I'm not in a hurry. Let me ask you something.
smallstory.L5-003: What made you open a shop like this?
smallstory.L5-101: Money. Had to find some kind of work.
smallstory.L5-103: But the numbers can't be the only thing that gets you opening up every day.
smallstory.L5-201: I like fixing things. Feels good when they work again.
smallstory.L5-203: I've spent my whole life around this stuff.
smallstory.L5-301: I wanted a place of my own.
smallstory.L5-302: All the more reason to keep it open.
smallstory.L5-303: It can be a mess. At least when you open the door, you know what you're doing that day.
smallstory.L5-901: When I first opened my shop, I had no idea what it'd become either.
smallstory.L5-902: Then the stock piled up, I got to know more people, and I just kept opening.
smallstory.L5-903: Keep yours going a while longer too.
smallstory.L5-904: So when I pass by, there's still somewhere to sit and talk.
smallstory.L5-G01: Busy again? Finish what you're doing. I'm in no hurry.
smallstory.L5-G02: Good, you're open. I thought you might be slacking off today.
smallstory.J1-001: What were you about to call me?
smallstory.J1-002: Don't be like those people. They hear who my dad is and suddenly they talk differently.
smallstory.J1-003: I have a name. Jiang Bai. Two words. That hard to remember?
smallstory.J1-103: Spare me the fancy titles from now on.
smallstory.J1-202: You're doing that on purpose, aren't you?
smallstory.J1-901: Enough talking. Are you looking at the goods I brought or what?
smallstory.J1-902: Pick something if you're buying. If not, I've got other places to be.
smallstory.J2-001: Can you find a plain fan around here?
smallstory.J2-002: T1, intact. Don't go straight for the most expensive one.
smallstory.J2-003: Find me one. You'll get your money.
smallstory.J2-103: Bring it to me when you find it.
smallstory.J2-201: Can't spare the time right now. I can't help.
smallstory.J2-203: Just don't shove some broken thing at me later.
smallstory.J2-304: Next time, then. I'm not rushing you.
smallstory.J2-311: You've been paid. Don't swap it for a more expensive one on my behalf.
smallstory.J2-312: Are you going to ask why I didn't just pick a better one too?
smallstory.J2-320: I said an intact T1 fan. Look again.
smallstory.J2-321: Leave it for now. The item and payment aren't sorted out yet.
smallstory.J2-401: You don't seem short of money.
smallstory.J2-402: I said plain. Why does everyone look at the price first?
smallstory.J2-403: If it costs more, you don't have to ask what I actually want?
smallstory.J2-501: Tell me what you want, and that's what I'll find.
smallstory.J2-503: Didn't think it was so hard to understand.
smallstory.J2-901: I'll decide what to do with it myself.
smallstory.J2-903: I've got the fan, and you've got the money. What else are you waiting for?
smallstory.J3-001: Are the fans in your server room still that loud?
smallstory.J3-002: My ears got some peace once I left.
smallstory.J3-003: Slept all right those days, though.
smallstory.J3-101: Weren't you always complaining about that lousy server room?
smallstory.J3-102: It was loud. I never said I couldn't sleep all night.
smallstory.J3-103: At least nobody woke me up at midnight asking what I was going to do with my life.
smallstory.J3-201: Give me some warning next time something happens.
smallstory.J3-202: I know. Stop going on about it.
smallstory.J3-203: There isn't always time to tell you.
smallstory.J3-901: I really did owe you for those few days.
smallstory.J3-902: I'm only saying it once. You heard me.
smallstory.J4-001: Someone just asked if I'd sell a box of old stuff a little cheaper.
smallstory.J4-101: What's in there that even you won't sell?
smallstory.J4-102: An old PC and a few photos.
smallstory.J4-201: Keep it safe if it means something to you.
smallstory.J4-203: But some people think a little more money makes everything negotiable.
smallstory.J4-901: Someone's waiting to have it back. What it's worth is another matter.
smallstory.J4-902: The goods I sell you follow the usual list. That box is separate.
smallstory.J5-002: Passing by. Thought I'd look in.
smallstory.J5-101: I thought you needed to hide out again.
smallstory.J5-103: Can't you imagine me coming here for anything else?
smallstory.J5-202: I can see that. You're finally not buried in a pile of parts.
smallstory.J5-203: Thought that was all you ever did.
smallstory.J5-901: No need to make room. Nothing for you to keep safe, either.
smallstory.J5-902: Just checking your shop is still open.
smallstory.J5-903: Get on with your customers. I'm not rushing you.
smallstory.J5-G01: Still alive? Good. Looks like this shop isn't closing anytime soon.
smallstory.J5-G02: Passing by. Thought I'd look in. Carry on.

serverroom.hardcore.guide_body_0:
1. Check cash, tonight's budget and the forecast first. After sleep, the base game's nightly costs are paid before machines are scheduled from remaining cash. Coins credited tomorrow cannot pay tonight's power bill.

2. Start with one T1 rig and retain operating cash. Check the chosen coin's algorithm, per-GPU VRAM requirement and difficulty. Cheap coins are not guaranteed to rebound; estimates change with prices, competition and power costs.

3. Upgrade power and cooling separately when expanding. Active server leases reserve capacity first. Rigs run by priority; if an expensive rig is unaffordable, later affordable rigs are still considered.

4. Reference value is only an estimate. Check executable net proceeds, fees, slippage and limits at the exchange. Only confirming a trade changes assets.
serverroom.hardcore.guide_body_1:
1. Rig Management -> Operating Details: select Eco, Standard or Overclock and set priority. Auto-downshift for capacity shortages must be enabled; otherwise insufficient capacity stops the rig.

2. Algorithm Details checks each installed GPU's actual VRAM. Several small cards cannot combine into one large card. Stop before changing parts. Removing and replacing a rig does not restore maintenance.

3. Prepare servicing below 60 maintenance. Below 30, overclock is disabled and rejection rises; zero causes protective shutdown. Stop, check Electronic Parts and the service fee, then service back to 100. Broken GPUs are not repaired.

4. In Mining Network, choose tomorrow's pool per coin. Steady deducts 2%; Variable deducts 0.5% with shared luck fluctuations. Existing balances remain; pool fees come from output, not cash.
serverroom.hardcore.guide_body_2:
1. Auto-sell defaults to Hold Coins. Cover Operations tries coins in your order to reach the next three nights' known rig-power budget. Fixed Share caps the sale at last night's new output x your percentage (0%-100%); source attribution still uses the whole wallet's proportions.

2. Each coin's minimum price uses actual whole-order net proceeds divided by quantity. Below-floor sales are skipped; limited depth sells only executable quantity and leaves the rest in the wallet. Costs are paid before automatic sales.

3. Order, percentage and price floors are a draft. Apply Draft and confirm to activate; Reload discards edits. Theme changes, minimizing and reopening retain the draft; switching saves clears it.

4. Separate production, cash and sources in the ledger. Prepaid rent is not earned rent, and fees are already included in cash. Actual equipment/repair costs are not fully tracked; exact payback is not promised.
serverroom.hardcore.guide_manual: Full illustrated guide: open the Computer Assembly and Trading Manual and read the server-room chapters. Forecasts use known current data and cannot guarantee future returns.
serverroom.hardcore.hardware_explain: Examples below use one intact catalog GPU of each tier, a matching-tier case, Standard mode and maintenance 100. They are not fully populated rigs or your installed equipment.
